english_translation: Pedestrians are crossing a busy road where cars travel, while small cars are parked along the side beside a bus terminus filled with many buses.

dialogue.shona: Vanhu vanoyambuka mugwagwa unofamba nemotokari.Parutivi pane motokari duku dzakamira uye pane chiteshi chinamabhazi akawanda.
dialogue.english: People are crossing a road used by cars; on the side small cars are parked near a bus station with many buses.

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('dzakamira')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'dzakamira' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('vanoyambuka')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'vanoyambuka' uses the present marker '-no-'. In Shona, inserting '-no-' between the subject prefix and the verb stem expresses general truths, everyday habits, or states of mind like 'wanting', 'thinking', and 'knowing'. For example: 'ndinoda' ('I want/like'), 'unofunga' ('you think'), 'vanoti' ('they say'), and 'vanorima' ('they farm').
grammar_notes.rule: [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('Parutivi')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'Parutivi'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Urban Bus Termini ('Chiteshi Chemabhazi') & Pedestrian Crossings
cultural_notes.content: Major urban bus stations ('zviteshi zvemabhazi') such as Charge Office, Fourth Street (Simon Vengayi Muzenda Street), and Market Square in Harare connect suburban commuters with long-distance buses travelling to every district of Zimbabwe.

active_exercises.prompt: Complete this sentence about travelling: 'Mangwana ______ bhazi rinoenda kuMasvingo.' (Tomorrow we will board the bus going to Masvingo.)
Translate this new sentence into English: 'Kombi chena iri kufamba pamugwagwa mukuru.'
options: The white minibus is travelling along the main road.
The large red truck is parked at the fuel station.
Two people are standing beside the shop in town.
Our journey to the mountains was long but enjoyable.
active_exercises.correct_answer: The white minibus is travelling along the main road.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Kombi chena' = 'The white minibus', 'iri kufamba' = 'is travelling', 'pamugwagwa mukuru' = 'along the main road'.

active_exercises.prompt: Your friend just passed her driving test! What do you say to congratulate her in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Makorokoto!' means 'Congratulations!' and 'nekubudirira kwako' means 'on your success'.
